>>>
# Welcome to Jank Diver Gaming
<<<
---
Welcome to the Jank Diver Peasant Cube!  Jank Diver Gaming is a Discord community focused on drafting our Peasant and JDG Mainline Historic cubes for Arena play, allowing us to cube with a growing group of friends from all over the world. This is an ever-evolving environment that takes both design goals AND player feedback. Our Discord community and Cube-centric podcast, The Jank Tank, can be found here:

>>>
https://discord.gg/6ncYbzU
<<<
>>>
https://open.spotify.com/show/1hZKYyIf5YicyEFz1o0ypS
<<<

The Peasant cube was Jank Diver Gaming’s original offering and grew out of the paper cube of one of the co-founders.  The cube was easy to port to Arena due to the designer’s chosen cardpool, Kaladesh-forward Standard sets.  The designer wanted to build a cube that drew from sets he had drafted in paper, having picked Magic back up in mid-2017.  

The Peasant cube is significantly more focused on two-color themes than the Mainline JDG Cube.  We feel that generating maximal power from uncommons is best accomplished by leaning into synergy and supporting focused strategies, since individual cards are not always extremely powerful in a vacuum. There is no Peasant equivalent to cards like [[Nissa, Who Shakes the World]] or [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]]. The following primer is an overview of the supported themes in each color pair. While alternative strategies can be drafted successfully, a streamlined deck in the pushed theme will usually have the best results.

>>>**Rules of Engagement**<<<

Speed: All array of different archetypes and match-ups. Respect fast starts and late-game engines equally. You likely need to do something starting on turn 2 at the latest to be competitive.
Balance: Balance is the designers' main goal for this cube. We want anyone to sit down at any seat, draft any color pair/strategy, and have a chance of winning the pod. We make changes and tweaks constantly based on experience and feedback.
Synergy: Aside from a few raw power cards, players are heavily rewarded for leaning into synergy and packages of cards. "Good-stuff" decks rarely win.
Removal: Waxes and wanes from season to season, though the cube has hit the high end of interaction lately. Removal is split between clean answers and more synergistic pieces that ask something of the player.
Land Destruction: There is a small chance that artifact lands can get sniped by an exile effect early in a game, but it's infrequent enough not to pose a real issue.
Alchemy: We've largely moved away from Alchemy designs after some negative experiences with them, though we reserve the right to play digital-only cards if we find them additive to the environment.

---
>>>
# Archetypes
<<<
---

>>>
**{U/W} Tempo**
<<<

<<[[!/Station Monitor]][[!/Sokka, Lateral Strategist]][[!/Floodpits Drowner]][[!/Aang, the Last Airbender]]>>

UW has been fully reworked multiple times in this cube, beginning as an overly-narrow fliers deck, morphing into a somewhat loose blink deck, and recently being refocused into a color pair that explicitly utilizes artifacts. The best way to describe the current iteration is Tempo, focused on disruptive bodies and cheap interaction. Some of the previous strategies like artifacts and blink are still partially supported.

>>>
**{U/B} Control**
<<<

<<[[!/The Bath Song]][[!/Behold the Unspeakable]][[!/Morbid Opportunist]][[!/Shoreline Looter]]>>

Blue-black has shifted away from all-in graveyard synergies, and is currently in "synergy limbo". It can be played as a control deck, combining blue's great card draw with black's efficient removal, but it can struggle closing out games or coming back from a lost boardstate. It's unfortunate that [[Invasion of Amonkhet]], one of Dimir's best cards, is a bit too overpowered for the environment. There are a few "draw cards" payoffs pulling together a Dimir subtheme, such as [[Sneaky Snacker]] and [[Foggy Swamp Spirit Keeper]].

>>>
**{B/R} Artifacts**
<<<

<<[[!/Marionette Apprentice]][[!/Oni-Cult Anvil]][[!/Dubious Delicacy]][[!/Improvised Club]]>>

While a little bit of Rakdos's aristocrats identity remains, the color pair has firmly moved towards artifacts as a central theme. "Artifact sacrifice" might be a more accurate description, leaning on sac outlets and payoffs for artifacts, mixed with burn damage from cards like [[Black Mage's Rod]] and [[Improvised Club]] for reach. This is a strong attrition deck that can morph around its opponent's plan post-sideboarding.

>>>
**{R/G} Stompy/Ramp**
<<<

<<[[!/Glacier Godmaw]][[!/Eldrazi Repurposer]][[!/Eomer of the Riddermark]][[!/Wandertale Mentor]]>>

RG stompy is one of the least-specific themes in the cube, offering a classic midrange attacking deck. Ramp isn't a huge feature of this cube, but Gruul naturally curves oversized creatures into one another, pressuring opponents and taxing removal. It's also been able to bridge out into a bit of a tokens gameplan lately, giving the color combo a bit more depth than it'd otherwise have.

>>>
**{G/W} Tokens**
<<<

<<[[!/Veteran Beastrider]][[!/A Killer Among Us]][[!Mighty Mutanimals]][[!Rosie Cotton of South Lane]]>>

GW was formerly a +1/+1 counter deck, but resulted in a glass cannon playstyle that used up cube equity for hyper-specific counter synergies. The theme has been scrapped in favor of a wider-reaching tokens theme, though we're still in search of a few excellent token payoffs in the cardpool. The color pair has had a strong resurgence lately, mostly off the back of white receiving tons of powerhouse cards throughout 2025 and 2026.

>>>
**{W/B} Grind/Recursion**
<<<

<<[[!/Ruthless Lawbringer]][[!/Lively Dirge]][[!/Sunpearl Kirin]][[!/Dune Drifter]]>>

BW is best described as the deck that's most interested in getting Ruthless Lawbringer into play as many times as possible each game. It brings together recursion elements with sacrifice texture to play a super grindy game that wins off chip advantages. This is the best "Skyfisher" deck and often bleeds into Esper territory for additional bounce + permanent-based synergy. Once a top-tier deck in the setting, we've cut back on self-bounce effects after reaching critical mass.

>>>
**{B/G} Food**
<<<

<<[[!/Tough Cookie]][[!/Back for Seconds]][[!/Vinereap Mentor]][[!/Bumi's Feast Lecture]]>>

Much like Dimir, Golgari has moved away from explicit graveyard synergies. Some of those still exist off the back of generic powerhouses like [[Honest Rutstein]], but the loudest theme for GB right now is Food. Mostly food as an artifact resource instead of food as a source of lifegain, though that always matters, too. 

>>>
**{G/U} Tempo/Ramp**
<<<

<<[[!/Repulsive Mutation]][[!/Ignis Scientia]][[!/Tyvar's Stand]][[!/Trumpeting Herd]]>>

Simic doesn't know what it wants to be in Peasant Cube. It has elements of ramp with few topend threats worth ramping into, and it has elements of artifacts-matter with few contributions of its own. It can play the tempo game off the back of strong X-spells like [[Repulsive Mutation]] and [[Tyvar's Stand]], plus 2-for-1s like [[Trumpeting Herd]], but it's always been and remains a confused color pair.

>>>
**{U/R} Artifacts**
<<<

<<[[!/Maverick Thopterist]][[!/Cryogen Relic]][[!/Sokenzan Smelter]][[!/Case of the Filched Falcon]]>>

Current Magic design has really eaten into instants and sorceries as an archetype in favor of noncreature spells and artifacts mattering more. Our Izzet section has followed that shift, and largely cares more about artifact synergies than "spell" payoffs, though some of those remain. There's significant overlap with red-black now, whereas Izzet used to overlap more directly with Dimir. This is indicative of a central shift away from the graveyard, and towards artifacts across the cube.

>>>
**{R/W} Go-Wide**
<<<

<<[[!/Arabella, Abandoned Doll]][[!/Mechanized Ninja Cavalry]][[!/Shocking Sharpshooter]][[!/Case of the Gateway Express]]>>

Aggro decks are at their best with a consistent, mono-color mana base in most unrestricted environments.  This is not the case here, and Boros aggro is more than the sum of its parts.  White and red both have access to a density of effects that produce wide boards and the means to pump them. Unlike most Peasant environments, 2/1 statlines don't play well here, so you really want your bodies to come attached with value plays, and then use anthem effects, timely removal, and raw power to push through wins. The best way to describe the current iteration of red-white is "Boros game objects".

>>>
**5-Color Decks**
<<<

We experimented recently with the addition of [[Everything Pizza]] and [[Snarl Song]], which have proven to be powerful enough role-players without making the entire cube dominated by multicolor decks. It's unclear right now how long we'll hold onto these, or if we'll add more, but they've earned a temporary spot here, despite our tendancies to shy away from 5-color incentives.

---
>>>
# Wrapping Up
<<<
---

We hope that you enjoyed this introduction to our environment.  We draft Peasant most Saturday afternoons at (2:30 P.M. EST) and our Mainline JDG Cube every Sunday at the same time. Rotating Rotisserie and Winston drafts organized by our active community members are also available and a great deal of fun.  There’s always something to do or discuss at Jank Diver Gaming, so come see what we’re all about and start divin'!

>>>
https://discord.gg/6ncYbzU
<<<

>>>
https://jankdivergaming.libsyn.com
<<<
